reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a personal Intel processor upgrade and performance discussion for gaming, video editing, and benchmarking. It also promotes a brand-provided giveaway requiring viewers to like, subscribe, and comment, with a randomly selected winner, and does not identify a request for payment, investment, credentials, or private data; whether the giveaway occurred or the prize was delivered remains unestablished.

citations.quote: recently I upgraded my PC with one of these the new Intel Core i9-9900k processor
it is about £500 though, so it's definitely not cheap
Intel are providing a brand new i7 8700K processor that's a six-core 12th red chip, brand new, and it can be yours to win!
All you have to do is click like and subscribe, it doesn't matter if you're already subscribed just make sure you are, and leave a comment
in the next couple of weeks I'll pick a winner at random

opening.argument: Judge, the giveaway is not merely background to a processor discussion. The presenter offers a brand-new processor as something the viewer can win, then states that liking, subscribing, and commenting are all they have to do. That is a direct exchange: audience engagement for a chance at a valuable reward. The promised random selection does not establish that a winner was selected or received the processor. The solicitation is the promise-action pairing, even without a request for money.

citations.quote: Intel are providing a brand new i7 8700K processor that's a six-core 12th red chip, brand new, and it can be yours to win!
All you have to do is click like and subscribe, it doesn't matter if you're already subscribed just make sure you are, and leave a comment
in the next couple of weeks I'll pick a winner at random

rebuttal.rebuttal: The processor discussion and price caveat do not erase the separate request for engagement in return for a chance to win. Nor does the absence of a payment or credentials request answer whether the reward claim is being used to obtain likes, subscriptions, and comments. The defense itself acknowledges that delivery is unestablished; the stated plan to pick a winner is a promise, not evidence that the giveaway was completed.

citations.quote: All you have to do is click like and subscribe, it doesn't matter if you're already subscribed just make sure you are, and leave a comment
in the next couple of weeks I'll pick a winner at random

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those quotes establish an ordinary stated giveaway with entry actions, not a deceptive reward scheme. The presenter says Intel provided the processor, describes random selection, and asks for likes, subscriptions, and a comment; he gives no payment or private-data step. Lack of later delivery evidence cannot itself establish that the stated giveaway was false.

citations.quote: Intel are providing a brand new i7 8700K processor
All you have to do is click like and subscribe, it doesn't matter if you're already subscribed just make sure you are, and leave a comment
in the next couple of weeks I'll pick a winner at random

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together: the description discloses that Intel supplied the CPU for the video, the presenter offers another Intel-supplied processor as a prize, and viewers are told to act through likes, subscriptions, and comments before a winner is picked in the next couple of weeks. That combination uses sponsor credibility, an easy entry path, and a near-term drawing to encourage immediate engagement. The description also contains shopping links, though the evidence does not make those links a giveaway-entry route. The concern is the reward-driven solicitation, not an invented fee or external claim process.

Intel are providing a brand new i7 8700K processor that's a six-core 12th red chip, brand new, and it can be yours to win!
All you have to do is click like and subscribe, it doesn't matter if you're already subscribed just make sure you are, and leave a comment
in the next couple of weeks I'll pick a winner at random
Help support the channel when shopping! Amazon US: http://amzn.to/2qSHDlp Amazon UK: http://amzn.to/2qg29NZ

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's point that the video discusses genuine processor uses addresses its subject, not the combined effect of sponsor backing, a prize, simple engagement steps, and a near-term drawing. A disclosed sponsor is not proof of deception, but neither does disclosure verify the promised selection or delivery. The lack of a money request narrows the concern; it does not remove the incentive to give the channel engagement for a chance at hardware.

citations.quote: BIG thanks to Intel for providing the CPU to make this video possible!
All you have to do is click like and subscribe, it doesn't matter if you're already subscribed just make sure you are, and leave a comment
in the next couple of weeks I'll pick a winner at random

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited signals are disclosed sponsorship, shopping links, and a giveaway with stated entry steps. They do not show a false prize, a manipulated drawing, or a claim that shopping is required to enter. The presenter explicitly credits Intel for making the video possible, while the giveaway instructions ask only for likes, a subscription, and a comment. Combining visible promotional elements does not establish deception.

citations.quote: BIG thanks to Intel for providing the CPU to make this video possible!
All you have to do is click like and subscribe, it doesn't matter if you're already subscribed just make sure you are, and leave a comment
Help support the channel when shopping! Amazon US: http://amzn.to/2qSHDlp Amazon UK: http://amzn.to/2qg29NZ

opening.argument: Judge, the technical discussion creates a reason to trust the presenter: he explains who might not need the expensive upgrade and reports his own editing-performance gain. But the video also explicitly pivots back to a giveaway, where the viewer's next step is to like, subscribe, and comment for a chance at a processor. The description thanks Intel for supplying the CPU used to make the video. Read as a whole, the educational presentation also serves a promotional goal: it builds attention and credibility before converting viewers into giveaway participants. The credible technical material does not validate the promised reward.

citations.quote: Now this isn't a review video or me saying that everyone should rush out and buy an i9 processor because they are expensive, and frankly, for a lot of people, they are going to be overkill.
i found that the i9 9900k was around 20 faster than the i7-8700K.
But back to the giveaway.
All you have to do is click like and subscribe, it doesn't matter if you're already subscribed just make sure you are, and leave a comment
BIG thanks to Intel for providing the CPU to make this video possible!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the upgrade discussion as the video's defining purpose. Yet the presenter expressly returns to the giveaway and asks viewers to subscribe, like, and comment. His warning that an i9 may be overkill can make the discussion more credible, but it does not verify the separate prize offer. Showing legitimate technical content answers whether the video is informative; it does not resolve whether that content also steers viewers into a reward-based solicitation.

citations.quote: for a lot of people, they are going to be overkill.
But back to the giveaway.
All you have to do is click like and subscribe, it doesn't matter if you're already subscribed just make sure you are, and leave a comment

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A video can contain promotion without being deceptive. The cited discussion gives concrete reasons for the upgrade, acknowledges that the i9 is expensive and excessive for many viewers, and identifies the brand contribution. The giveaway is presented openly with simple entry steps. Reframing those disclosed elements as a conversion effort does not show that the prize promise is false or that viewers are being misled.
